prop:chirality-sign-is-hypercharge-sign:
Proposition The chirality sign is the hypercharge sign. Proposition. On five strands with charge Q(\alpha) = T_3 + \alpha Y_0, Y_0 = (-2,-2,-2,3,3):

  1. Q(-\alpha)_S = -Q(\alpha)_{s(S)}, where s swaps the two isospin strands; hence the even part at -\alpha has the charge spectrum of the odd part at \alpha. The two open signs, which part is matter and which root \alpha = \pm 1/6 of prop:neutral-lepton-fixes-charges, are one sign: only their product is physical;
  2. at \alpha = 1/6 strand 4 is neutral, and S \mapsto S \,\triangle\, \{4\} is a bijection from the even part to the odd part that preserves electric charge and fixes the colour strands. Colour and electric charge cannot see the sign;
  3. six even states have Y_0 = 1 and no odd state does, so no bijection between the two parts preserves hypercharge.

So the chirality sign is the sign of hypercharge relative to the matter part. It is a weak-sector datum, as expected: the strong and electromagnetic sectors are vector-like.

Proof. Item 1 is qWeight5_neg summed over S, then reindexing by s and the complement bijection of prop:even-strand-generation. Item 2: adding or removing a neutral strand does not change the charge, and toggling one strand flips parity. Item 3 is a count over the thirty-two subsets.

What stays open. The value of the single remaining sign.

prop:linking-does-not-fix-charge:

  1. the leptons e = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1, \mu = \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^{-1}, \tau = \sigma_1^4\sigma_2^{-1} have linking sums 2, 2, 4 and all carry charge -1;

  3. mirroring the electron word negates its linking sum and leaves its strand permutation unchanged.

So the linking sign is the handedness of the braid, a parity-type datum, while the open sign of prop:chirality-sign-is-hypercharge-sign is a charge-conjugation-type datum (Y \mapsto -Y). The linking number, alone, does not fix it.

Proof. Finite computation on the words.

prop:strand-slot-separates-gen1:
Proposition The strand slot separates the first-generation quark states. Proposition. Place each first-generation quark state in one of four slots on 5 = C \oplus V: a single colour strand in \bar 5, or a strand pair of type colour\wedge e_3, colour\wedge e_4 or colour\wedgecolour in \Lambda^2 5, by the Georgi–Glashow assignment u_L, \bar u_L \mapsto colour\wedge e_3, d_L, \bar d_L \mapsto colour\wedge e_4, u_R, \bar u_R \mapsto colour\wedgecolour, d_R, \bar d_R \mapsto colour. Mark the states \bar u_L, \bar d_L, u_R, d_R as dual, meaning they sit in 5 \oplus \Lambda^2 \bar 5.

  1. Slot and dual flag together separate all eight states; the slot alone does not.
  2. The dual flag is set exactly when the chirality bit and the particle bit differ.
  3. At \alpha = \tfrac16 the slot charges are \tfrac13, \tfrac23, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac23, independent of the colour strand. Negated on dual states, they give +\tfrac23 on u, -\tfrac13 on d, and the negatives on \bar u, \bar d.

Proof. Items 1 and 2 are a case check over the eight states. Item 3 is the neutral-lepton proposition at \alpha = \tfrac16. \square

Scope. The chirality analysis in ChiralityIndependentOfCrossing shows the crossing sign cannot separate the sector and leaves one further label open. This proposition takes that label to be the strand slot. The slot assignment is the Georgi–Glashow embedding and is an input; so are the matter content, one neutral lepton and Fermi exchange, through the Fermi pair proposition.
prop:slot-from-even-shape:
Proposition The quark slot is the shape of an even strand subset. Proposition. Split the five strands of 5 = C \oplus V into colour C = \{0,1,2\} and isospin V = \{3,4\}, and call an even subset S a quark state when 1 \le |S \cap C| \le 2. Then:

  1. the quark states are exactly the twelve subsets \{c,3\}, \{c,4\}, \{c,c+1\} and \{c\}^c for c \in C (indices of c+1 mod 3), all different; the other four even subsets \varnothing, \{3,4\}, \{3\}^c, \{4\}^c are colour singlets;
  2. at \alpha = 1/6 the charges y_S of these four shapes are +2/3, -1/3, -2/3, +1/3, independent of c, and they are the charges slotCharge assigns to the slots colour\wedge 3, colour\wedge 4, colour\wedgecolour and colour;
  3. these four charges are distinct, so any assignment of slots to the eight first-generation quark states that reproduces their charges, with the dual flag as sign, is the Georgi–Glashow assignment of prop:strand-slot-separates-gen1.

So the slot is the shape of an even subset, and the Georgi–Glashow embedding [baez-huerta2010] is no longer an input once matter is the even part (prop:even-strand-generation). The degree-4 shape \{c\}^c carries the \bar 5 charge -y_c by complementation; the \bar 5 is not put in separately.

rem:cal2-higgs-knot-coupling:
Remark The muon-ratio aether proxy as a Higgs-knot volume coupling. The canonical particle–knot table assigns the figure-eight knot 4_1 to the Higgs boson — an assignment with structural content of its own, since 4_1 is amphichiral, matching a scalar that is its own antiparticle. Read against that table, the muon-to-electron aether relation

  \frac{\mathfrak{m}_\mu}{\mathfrak{m}_e} \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}

acquires a sharp interpretation: the muon's mass is the electron scale dressed by the Higgs knot's hyperbolic volume. What the Standard Model phrases as "the muon acquires mass through its Yukawa coupling to the Higgs field" the framework phrases as "the muon's mass proxy evaluates the volume of the Higgs knot" — the same structural role, played by \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299 rather than a fitted Yukawa constant.

Two boundaries delimit this reading. First, it is interpretive: the identity is the weak-modulus aether calibration proxy, established independently of the table, and nothing new is derived by the relabelling. Second, the muon's identity knot remains the cinquefoil 5_1; the figure-eight enters the mass formula as the coupling object, not as the muon itself — the same division of roles the nucleon chain exhibits, where the mass-bearing volume (\mathcal{B}_3) is not the identity knot of any single constituent.
rem:a5-orbital-degeneracy-fracture:
Remark Orbital degeneracies fracture along A_5 irreducibles. If the archimedean truncation of the truncation conjecture is the right picture — observable-scale symmetry descending from the fibre's discrete automorphisms rather than a continuous rotation group — then atomic orbital degeneracies inherit a specific discrete fingerprint. Restricting the (2l+1)-dimensional \mathrm{SO}(3) representations to the icosahedral group A_5 \subset S_5 (the orientation-preserving automorphisms of the Bring fibre) gives, by exact character arithmetic:

orbital 2l+1 A_5 decomposition
s 1 \mathbf{1}
p 3 \mathbf{3}
d 5 \mathbf{5}
f 7 \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4}
g 9 \mathbf{4} \oplus \mathbf{5}
h 11 \mathbf{3} \oplus \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{5}

The s, p, d degeneracies are native — they are exactly the dimensions 1, 3, 5 of A_5 irreducibles and restrict irreducibly. Every degeneracy above five fractures: the group has no irreducible of dimension greater than 5, so the f orbital's seven states are, under the truncated symmetry, a composite of a \mathbf{3}' and a \mathbf{4} that a continuous rotation group would hold together. The branching arithmetic is standard finite-group representation theory, computed exactly.

The physical reading — that f-shell degeneracy is only approximate, with a fine-structure split along the \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4} seam — is conditional on the truncation conjecture and is recorded here as an interpretive consequence, not a prediction wired to any computation.

No falsifiability claim is made. One might argue that a truncated discrete symmetry cannot hold seven states exactly degenerate, while exact \mathrm{SO}(3) can, so the two pictures differ "at some resolution" on lanthanide-scale spectroscopy. Two objections. First, free-atom f-shell structure is already described to spectroscopic precision by rotationally invariant theory: states are labelled by J with (2J+1) degeneracy exact by isotropy, and the observed lifting is spin--orbit, in a J pattern rather than along a \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4} seam. Second, and more fundamental, "at some resolution" names no resolution. The statement is compatible with every null result, which makes it untestable rather than falsifiable.

What is missing sits upstream of any bound. The branching establishes that the seam exists; it fixes no splitting magnitude, and none follows from character arithmetic alone. The experiment that would constrain such a splitting is itself undetermined, because the framework does not say how the icosahedral frame attaches to space:

  • if the A_5 frame is fixed in space, the atomic Hamiltonian is anisotropic, so the binding constraint is the Hughes--Drever family of clock-comparison tests of rotational invariance, which are far tighter than any lanthanide measurement;
  • if each atom carries an independently oriented frame, the anisotropy averages out and the constraint is line structure in an ensemble spectrum, which is the lanthanide measurement.

Until that is specified one cannot choose the experiment, let alone compute a bound. Supplying it is the open item here, ahead of any spectroscopic campaign.

This is a scope-(a) objection. The branching arithmetic stands: the six rows above were re-derived independently by \mathrm{SO}(3) \downarrow A_5 character arithmetic and reproduce exactly. Nothing here excludes the truncation picture. What is withdrawn is the claim that this block's value lies in falsifiability.
prose:sm-params-intro:
The 26 parameters of the Standard Model.

A derivation of the Standard Model must ultimately account for its free parameters. In the counting used here, the renormalisable Standard Model carries 19 parameters — 9 charged-fermion masses, 4 quark-mixing (CKM) parameters, 3 gauge couplings, 2 Higgs-sector parameters, and the strong-CP angle — and the neutrino-sector extension adds 7 more (3 masses, 3 mixing angles, 1 Dirac CP phase), for a total of 26. If the neutrinos are Majorana, two further phases appear; they are noted in the neutrino section and not counted in the 26.

The following sections walk the 26 parameters in chunks, one section per chunk, and record for each parameter its status in the framework using the tiers of the appendix introduction: input (one of the three calibration observables, not a prediction), proxy (a calibration proxy, exact by construction under the canonical pin), partial (a derived or conditional structure exists but the parameter is not closed), conjectural (a precise identification exists without derivation), and open (nothing here closes the parameter).

The headline count is stated up front so that the chunk tables cannot be misread as progress claims: of the 26 parameters, 1 is an input (m_e, the dimensional unit), 1 is a calibration proxy (m_\mu, pinning the aether modulus through the \beta-sector bar-skew calibration), 1 is partial (\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}, conditional structure with open per-loop measure), 2 are conjectural (\sin^2\theta_W, m_H), and 21 are open. No parameter beyond the calibration set is currently derived to experimental precision.
prose:sm-params-lepton-masses:
Charged-lepton masses (3).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_e input — the dimensional unit calibration triple
m_\mu proxy for the \beta-sector bar-skew calibration; as a proton-pinned prediction it misses the per-observable target by 970.2\times m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2
m_\tau open — no knot identification; the direct volume reading is refuted over a 25-knot search tau knot prediction

The electron mass is the framework's dimensional unit and is an input, not a prediction. The muon mass is the numerical proxy for the neutron \beta-sector bar-skew calibration P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}: the ratio m_\mu/m_e \approx \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 pins the aether modulus q_0, so under the canonical (muon) pin the muon mass is exact by construction — a calibration tautology, not an accuracy result. Under the experimental (proton) pin, m_\mu becomes a genuine prediction and misses its hundredfold-experimental-precision target by 970.2\times (211.2 ppb against a target of 0.2177 ppb), the \mu–p aether tension recorded in the precision-goals ledger. Either way, m_\mu does not count as a derived Standard-Model parameter.

The tau mass is open, and the obvious route has a recorded negative: the tau knot-prediction remark reports that a direct search over 25 hyperbolic knots found no K_\tau with m_\tau/m_e \approx \mathrm{Vol}(K_\tau)/\hbar_q^{k_\tau} within one percent — a scope-limited refutation of the naive volume reading as tested, not an exclusion of a tau carrier altogether. The framework does treat the tau's decay structure through the T(3,5) weak vertex — the tau leptonic-universality proposition derives lepton universality of the leptonic branching ratios from the Hecke amplitude's independence of the daughter lepton — but universality of ratios is not a mass. The missing object is the tau's carrier identification, together with whatever correction to the direct volume reading the 25-knot negative is pointing at.
prose:sm-params-quark-masses:
Quark masses (6).

Parameter Framework status
m_u, m_d open — quarks are composite constituents, not independent inputs
m_s, m_c open
m_b, m_t open

All six quark masses are open, and the framework's structural position makes the question different in kind from the Standard Model's. In the Standard Model the quark masses are six independent Yukawa couplings; in the framework, light quarks are not elementary inputs but components of composite braids — the up and down quarks appear as constituent structure of the Borromean baryon braid, with the proton–neutron split carried by an isospin assignment layer rather than by two independent masses. A constituent-level density (the structural identity relating the constituent density to the three-strand Markov trace) exists at the baryon level, but no construction extracts individual current-quark masses m_u, \ldots, m_t from it, and the heavy flavours are untouched here: no knot or braid identification exists for s, c, b, or t as mass carriers.

In sum: the framework currently predicts baryon-level masses and proposes to treat quark masses as derived constituent data, but the derivation of any individual quark mass — light or heavy — is open, and it is not yet established that the six current-quark masses are even the natural parameters of the framework's flavour sector.

This suggests the correct target is operational rather than definitional. Experimentally, no quark mass is measured directly: light-quark masses are scheme-dependent parameters extracted by inverting hadron spectroscopy through lattice computation and chiral perturbation theory, heavy-quark masses come from quarkonium spectra, and only the top — which decays before hadronizing — is reconstructed from decay products. The framework therefore need not define m_q at all; it need only derive the observables that the extraction procedures consume, and may then run the equivalent extraction to produce scheme-comparable numbers. Two consequences fix the programme. First, the cleanest extractable quantity is the isospin-breaking difference m_d - m_u: its experimental source is the neutron–proton splitting \Delta_{pn} after removing the electromagnetic self-energy, and the framework derives both \Delta_{pn} and its own electromagnetic–strong decomposition (the antisymmetric Coulomb crossing term of the Coulomb charge), so an extraction of "m_d - m_u in the framework scheme" is well-posed with no new inputs. Second, the combination m_u + m_d is not honestly extractable this way: its experimental source is m_\pi^2, and the charged-pion mass m_{\pi^\pm} is a physical calibration input — so any extraction through it would be circular. The parameters this section tabulates are thus reinterpreted: not six numbers the framework owes, but six scheme quantities of the observer's inversion procedure, of which the framework can currently ground one difference and must remain silent on the calibration-tainted combinations.
prose:sm-params-ckm:
Quark mixing (4).

Parameter Framework status
\theta_{12} (Cabibbo) open
\theta_{23}, \theta_{13} open
\delta_{\mathrm{CKM}} open — CP violation surveyed observationally only

All four CKM parameters are open. This paper records the experimental evidence for CP violation and the role of the complex phase \delta_{\mathrm{CKM}} in the observations chapter, and a spectral-form section discusses where a CP-violating phase could live in the categorical structure; but no categorical object has been constructed whose matrix elements yield a mixing matrix, no Cabibbo angle is derived, and there is no candidate mechanism relating the three mixing angles to braid or knot data.

The structural prerequisite is visible from the flavour discussion in the quark-mass section: a mixing matrix presupposes a flavour basis, and the framework has not yet fixed what its flavour degrees of freedom are beyond the isospin doublet. Until the flavour sector is defined categorically, the CKM parameters are not merely uncomputed — they are unposed.
prose:sm-params-gauge-couplings:
Gauge couplings (3).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} partial — conditional fixed-point structure; per-loop measure open EM-coupling fixed point, Habiro bar-involution
\sin^2\theta_W conjectural Weinberg angle, categorical
\alpha_s open strong-sector anchors are conjectural identifications

The electromagnetic coupling is the most developed of the three. A conditional fixed-point equation for \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} exists — the EM-coupling fixed-point proposition is a theorem conditional on a named normalization class — and the fibre-level Habiro structure of the coupling is treated in the bar-involution proposition. What remains open is recorded in the derivation-status remark: the per-loop measure is not derived, so \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} is partial, not closed. Reporting it as derived would launder the conditional hypothesis into an established premise.

Numerically the assembled form is the framework's closest approach to any Standard-Model parameter, and it is stated here so that the partial tier is not mistaken for an absence of content. Writing g = 4 for the genus of Bring's surface and taking the crossing numbers of T(2,9) and T(3,5),

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}}
  \;=\;
  q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q \;+\; \frac{2g}{4\pi(g-1)}
  \;+\; \alpha H\,(1 - h^2\alpha) \;+\; \Delta_2,
  \qquad
  H = \frac{[2]_q}{8\pi},
  \qquad
  h = q - q^{-1}.

The symbol \alpha appears on both sides, so the relation is self-consistent rather than a series in an auxiliary small parameter, and it is solved as a fixed point. The \alpha-dependent part is written out rather than abbreviated to O(\alpha) because it is not an unspecified remainder: to the order currently derived it is exactly \alpha H(1 - h^2\alpha), in which h is the Hecke structure constant of the Hecke-algebra convention — the denominator of the balanced [k]_q — and not the mass-chain quantity \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, from which it differs by a factor of about 2.11. Truncating after \alpha H gives a quadratic fixed point and a residual of 1.67 parts per billion at the experimental (proton) pin; retaining the cubic Schwinger factor (1 - h^2\alpha) gives 0.313 ppb, about 2.1 times the experimental uncertainty \sigma_\alpha \approx 0.15 ppb. Both residuals are measured against the caesium-recoil determination \alpha^{-1} = 137.035999084 (CODATA 2018), which the corpus retains as a deliberate choice of determination; the CODATA 2022 value is 137.035999177. Under the ideal (muon) pin — the muon anchor derived from the current CODATA lepton ratio rather than the earlier frozen value, which gave 80.51 — the quadratic form gives 81.04 ppb instead. Every integer entering the form is structurally fixed — the genus and two crossing numbers — and no coefficient is fitted.

The genuine remainder is \Delta_2, the uncomputed archimedean two-loop term. It is not the -h^2H\alpha^2 piece already carried in the form above: that piece is weight one, a q-rational over \pi, whereas the two-loop object is weight three of \zeta(3) type, roughly forty times larger, and lives on the archimedean side of the wall rather than in the fibre. Its coefficient is c_2 \approx 8.1 \times 10^{-4}, which is not the Ohtsuki \kappa_1 \approx 0.554; the two differ by nearly three orders of magnitude and identifying them would be an error. Measured against the hundredfold-experimental-precision criterion, which asks for \sigma_\alpha/100 \approx 0.0015 ppb, the cubic form remains about 209 times short — close by the standards of this framework, and not yet at target.

None of the qualifications attached to that figure is discharged. The derivation passes through three unproved classes, so the result is conditional throughout; and because the leading term alone misses by more than 5 \times 10^5 times the assembled residual, the agreement is a property of the complete form rather than of any single ingredient within it. The anchor choice, moreover, is the residual. The 78.84 ppb spread between the two pins is roughly 47 times the proton-anchored figure, and no anchor-blind correction of order \alpha can absorb it, so what appears here is the muon–proton aether tension of the three-calibration-discipline proposition surfacing in a second observable. What keeps the agreement from being anchor-shopping is that the proton pin was adopted on precision grounds independently of, and prior to, this calculation; that independence is also what allows \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} to serve as a second witness for the pin. The per-loop measure, finally, remains underived, and it is that omission which bars the parameter from any tier above partial.

The weak mixing angle has a precise categorical candidate — the Weinberg-angle conjecture — but it is a conjecture, and its inputs overlap the conjectural electroweak isotypic structure of the truncation conjecture; it inherits, in particular, the open hypercharge problem, since \theta_W mixes exactly the two \mathrm{U}(1)'s the framework has not yet separated.

Two numbers circulate for this parameter and they measure different things, so neither refutes the other. Evaluating the conjecture's trace ratio at the pure pattern gives \cot\theta_W \approx 0.659 against a CODATA target near 1.823 — the roughly sixty-percent miss the conjecture block reports. A separate construction on the (3,2,1) Wedderburn block reaches 1.8208, a residual of 0.127\%. The smaller figure must not be cited as a framework accuracy result. Its own computational witness declines to support it: the residual factor was selected as the closest of 74 enumerated candidates, the best of them missing the required 1.02239 by 1.3 \times 10^{-3}, and the witness records the ansatz as neither supported at 10^{-3} nor falsified at 10^{-2} — an explicitly inconclusive verdict. The surviving exponent is expressible as a corner hook of (3,2,1), which makes it structurally available; availability after a proximity search is not derivation, and the sweep ranged well beyond the hooks. The parameter therefore stays conjectural.

A second ground bears on the same figure, and it is the stronger of the two because it does not depend on how the exponent was chosen. (3,2,1) has three rows, and the Schur–Weyl row cap gives \dim V_\lambda = 0 whenever \ell(\lambda) > N; the fibre is the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), so N = 2 and that block carries no states. Its Ocneanu weight vanishes identically, which is why the conjecture's own trace ratio — built from \mathrm{tr}_M, and so blind to the block by construction — cannot reach 1.8208 at all. The two numbers are therefore not competing estimates of one quantity: one is computed inside the carrier and one outside it. Every route from such a block to a physical number is either a Markov trace, which the row cap sends to zero, or a spectrum, which has no states to act on; a quantity recovered by subtraction is a difference of Markov traces and so, by linearity, is itself the first kind. Deriving the exponent would therefore not close the gap — the reading would remain outside the carrier whatever the exponent turned out to be.

The tractable lever is elsewhere. The Milnor triple linking number \bar\mu_{123} supplies the writhe-independent second crossing invariant and separates the two \mathrm{U}(1)'s; what it does not yet supply is their relative coupling normalisation, which inherits the open flavour \mathrm{SU}(3) sector.

The strong coupling is open. The torus-knot anchors assigned to the strong sector are themselves conjectural identifications, and no construction extracts a coupling constant from them; there is no candidate formula for \alpha_s at any scale, and no analogue of the fixed-point equation exists for the colour sector — unsurprisingly, since the \mathrm{SU}(3) action itself is open.
prose:sm-params-higgs:
Higgs sector (2).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_H conjectural — T(2,8) torus-link identification; conditional Plancherel-trace ratio formula electroweak triplet
v (electroweak scale) open — competing conditional fixed-point and four-hop weak-jet scalings electroweak triplet

The Higgs mass has a conjectural identification: the Higgs is assigned the torus link T(2,8) within the electroweak triplet conjecture, alongside W = T(2,4) and Z = T(2,6). Because torus links have zero hyperbolic volume, their mass chain rests on two-strand Plancherel trace polynomials P_m(h) (h = q - q^{-1}) rather than hyperbolic volume. Dressing the W \to Z genus step by ([2]_q/2)^2 = 1 + h^2/4 reconciles the W- and Z-anchored mass ratios (m_Z/m_W within 175 parts per million of experiment) and places the (6/5)-scaled P_4(h_0)/P_2(h_0) scalar-to-gauge ratio near 125.1–125.5\;\mathrm{GeV} (corresponding to a positive tree-level Higgs quartic \lambda_H = m_H^2/(2v^2) \approx 0.129), whereas omitting the quantum-dimension dressing leaves a -0.66\% (124.37\;\mathrm{GeV}) residual under the Borromean 2G h_0^4 correction. Because neither the 6/5 prefactor nor the higher-order loop factor is derived from the category, the parameter remains conjectural.

The electroweak scale v remains open, with two distinct structural routes in tension. First, on the noncommutative Sweedler weak first jet, a four-hop charged-current contraction carries scaling (q_0^2 - 1)^8 \approx 8.41 \times 10^{-6} against G_F \mathfrak{m}_p^2 \approx 1.03 \times 10^{-5} (-18.1\%, or +10.5\% on v \approx 272.1\;\mathrm{GeV} under direct Frobenius-norm identification), whereas interpreting (q_0^2 - 1)^8 as a squared weak decay rate scales G_F \mathfrak{m}_p^2 as (q_0^2 - 1)^4 and underpredicts v by more than an order of magnitude at the proton scale (14.65\;\mathrm{GeV}). Second, the conditional Bring–Schwinger fixed-point cubic 1/\alpha_v = q([2]_q/2)[4]_q[6]_q[8]_q + 1/\pi - \alpha_v H(1 - \hbar_q^2\alpha_v) (H = [2]_q/(8\pi)) matches v/\mathfrak{m}_p to -29.4 parts per billion (and to +81.1 parts per billion without cubic iteration when the loop coupling is fixed to the parameter-free Sweedler factor 2^{1/4}(q_0^2 - 1)^4 < 1/30, avoiding the \alpha_2 > 1/30 incompatibility), yet rests on undischarged selections for the dressing exponent, the per-carrier zero-mode rule, and the \mathrm{SU}(2)_L loop sign. Because v normalises every Standard-Model mass via the Yukawa mechanism inside the G-action-on-aether conjecture, reconciling this open electroweak scale with the calibrated volume–density and Hecke-energy mass chains remains an essential obligation.
prose:sm-params-theta-qcd:
The strong-CP angle (1).

Parameter Framework status
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}} open — no construction offered here

The strong-CP angle is entirely open: nothing in this paper predicts \theta_{\mathrm{QCD}} or solves the strong-CP problem. One speculative direction can be named without endorsement: the framework's framing phase q^{w \cdot c} is a topological angle attached to crossings, which is the same kind of object as a \theta-term, and its per-crossing coupling is already structurally fixed at c = 1/2 by the Coulomb-charge definition. Whether the observed smallness of \theta_{\mathrm{QCD}} could arise from the framing sector is a question, not a claim; the framing phase's derived readings (charge and isospin) are already spoken for, and a full derivation would first require the \mathrm{SU}(3) sector itself, which is open.

Within this direction, one algebraic step holds unconditionally. Charge conjugation acts on the Hecke fibre as the bar-involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, which on the aether circle is complex conjugation; so a colour sector whose total framing phase is bar-symmetric (CP-even) would have a real framing phase, forcing \theta_{\mathrm{QCD}} \in \{0, \pi\}. That reality implication is proved over a generic base ring. It is not a solution: the CP-evenness hypothesis is undischarged — a single T(2,9) gluon knot has writhe 9 \neq 0 and is maximally chiral, so CP-evenness would need a colour-singlet writhe cancellation over the 9 = 3 \times 3 tube structure, which requires the \mathrm{SU}(3) sector, itself open. Moreover \{0, \pi\} is a discrete prediction, not the observed |\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}| < 10^{-10} smallness, which remains open.
prose:sm-params-neutrino:
Neutrino sector (7).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_{\nu_1}, m_{\nu_2}, m_{\nu_3} open — carrier identified, mass mechanism absent neutrino knot, antineutrino knot
\theta_{12}, \theta_{23}, \theta_{13} (PMNS) open —
\delta_{\mathrm{CP}} (PMNS) open —

The neutrino has a carrier identification: the neutrino-knot definition assigns it the unknot, with the antineutrino as its mirror datum. The unknot has zero hyperbolic volume, so the volume–density mass chain gives the neutrino zero mass — consistent with near-masslessness at leading order, but by the same token the framework currently contains no mechanism for the small nonzero masses that oscillation data require. The three mass eigenvalues (equivalently two splittings and an absolute scale) are open, and the framework does not yet distinguish Dirac from Majorana character; on a Majorana reading two additional phases join the count and are equally open.

All four PMNS parameters are open, for the same structural reason as the CKM sector: mixing presupposes a flavour basis, and no categorical flavour structure exists for the three neutrino generations — indeed the framework has no three-generation structure at all yet, for leptons or quarks. The generation-counting problem (why three copies?) is prior to every parameter in this table and is addressed in this paper only as an open item; it belongs on any list of what a Standard-Model derivation from this framework must eventually produce.

Not yet stated in any chapter: the weak-isospin grading T_3, the T_3 selection of meson operators, the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} form ladder and its anchor dominance, and the stage-1 quark-mass extraction scoping.

The dominant mode of contribution is deletion

A reader asking what these derivations give should be told this first. The surface carries five self-withdrawals and several proved negatives against one derived entry, and the negatives are worth more. Gell-Mann–Okubo, the decuplet equal-spacing rule behind the \Omega^- prediction, and the Coleman–Glashow relation are each proved to hold identically for any first-order octet breaking. Reproducing them is therefore evidence for nothing, and removing them as derivation targets is a larger contribution than most positive results would have been, because it stops a zero-information success from being counted as one.

The testable content is what remains: their deviations, respectively about 6\%, 9.2\% and 0.8\%. The framework derives no second-order term, so it predicts zero for all three.
prose:sm-gating-objects:
The open parameters funnel into three missing objects.

The Standard Model's open parameters are not independent problems. Tracing each blocker backwards, they funnel into three missing objects. Closing any one of them would move a whole family of parameters at once, which is what makes the grouping worth stating rather than listing the parameters individually.

A three-dimensional flavour object

Gates every quark row, every hypercharge value, the meson octet, the baryon decuplet, every inter-multiplet mass splitting, the \eta', all four CKM angles, all four PMNS angles, \alpha_s, the smallness of \theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}, and the normalisation of \sin^2\theta_W.

The obstruction is established: the framework supplies a two-dimensional fundamental, and no choice of the deformation parameter raises that, since Drinfeld–Jimbo deformation does not change dimensions. What is missing is a construction. Several routes are excluded, each against a named invariant — among them Frobenius–Schur parity, which rules out every odd-dimensional summand of a tensor power of the two-dimensional fibre.

A caution about how the surviving question is posed. It has been recorded as asking whether a certain non-abelian cohomology class is non-trivial, and whether the resulting gerbe's band can be \mathrm{SU}(3). That formulation belongs to symmetric Tannakian duality [deligne1990], and this framework's category is not symmetric — a fact that follows from the Hecke relation together with q_0 > 1, rather than being stipulated. Reading the framework's own \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2) result as settling the band therefore assumes what is being asked. The general non-symmetric reconstruction produces a Hopf algebra internal to the category, not a group scheme carrying a band, so the question to ask is what that reconstructed Hopf algebra is, and whether it contains an \mathrm{SU}(3)-like sub-object.

This is a re-posing, not an exclusion. Nothing here says \mathrm{SU}(3) is absent.

The intra-nucleon electromagnetic self-energy

Gates the up–down quark mass difference. Its experimental source is the proton–neutron splitting minus the electromagnetic self-energy, and the framework derives the splitting; the self-energy is the open object. The only derived electromagnetic mechanism in the framework acts between nucleons, whereas this one acts within one.

Two structural facts constrain what can carry it. Every pairwise linking number vanishes on the Borromean braid that represents the nucleon, so the pairwise linking data of the proton is identical to that of the unlink and no functional of it can distinguish them. And the first invariant that does not vanish there, the Milnor triple linking number, reverses sign when the two like-charged components are exchanged — while a Coulomb self-energy between identical charges cannot. Any account odd in that invariant is therefore zero, which removes the linear ansatz before it is attempted.

This object gates one front, not two. It has been recorded as also owning part of the mirror-nucleus splitting. It does not: that splitting is a binding-energy difference, and a single nucleon's electromagnetic self-energy cancels identically in binding energy, since it already sits inside the free nucleon masses. The mirror front needs an inter-nucleon pair term; this front needs an intra-nucleon self-energy. They are different objects that happened to share a description.

The content-to-braid map

Gates the charmed-hadron spectrum, the strange and charm masses, the D-meson mass, hypercharge on strange states, and thereby the normalisation of \sin^2\theta_W.

No third flavour grade is missing. The winding together with weak isospin separates all six quarks, and that is proved. The residual collision between the two neutral mesons \bar D^0 and K^0 is an artefact of reading the graded content as a multiset: as ordered pairs, (-5, +3) and (+3, -5) are distinct, and the ordering is the quark–antiquark strand orientation — the same signed-writhe datum that supplies weak isospin. The map from mesons to ordered content is injective (a finite check, decided by computation), and the statement that the mass cannot be a function of the grading quantifies only over symmetric functions of the unordered content; it does not constrain a function of the ordered content. So this object does not reduce into the first. What remains is a canonical, parameter-free map from the ordered content to a hyperbolic braid word at H_3(q) — a geometric construction needing neither flavour nor colour \mathrm{SU}(3). Injectivity gives a factorisation of the mass through the content, never a derivation of the factorising map; a fit through five injectively labelled points is the per-state fit the charmonium attack already recorded as worthless.

sec:surreal-appendix-intro:
Motivation: a surreal-number ambient for QOU.

This appendix develops Conway's surreal numbers \mathbf{No} as a realisation of the Quantum Observable Universe alongside \mathbb{R} (or \mathbb{C}). \mathbf{No} is the unique proper-class real-closed field containing every ordered-field extension of \mathbb{R}, including the hyperreals ^{*}\mathbb{R}, the ordinals \mathrm{Ord}, and all Hahn series \mathbb{R}((t^{G})) [conway1976, ehrlich2012].

How this appendix relates to the rest of the paper. The paper is developed over a general commutative ring R, and its categorical results hold for every R at once (why not the real numbers). Neither \mathbb{R} nor \mathbf{No} is the native ground field: both are realisations applied at the end. The surreal realisation is the one that keeps the algebraic structure of an error term, naming infinitesimal and infinite errors as genuine elements instead of collapsing them to a real bound, and the classical statements are recovered from it by taking standard parts. The structure each use needs is graded in Lean. Infinitesimals, standard part and limit transfer need only an ordered field containing \mathbb{R} with an element above every natural number (SurrealBase, of which the hyperreals ^{*}\mathbb{R} are an instance). Birthday bounds add a birthday function (BirthdayField). Statements that use Conway simplicity need the full Conway structure (SurrealField), whose intended model is \mathbf{No}. The claims here are either remarks interpreting existing blocks, conjectures pending further development, or definitions of new auxiliary structures.

Motivation for the surreal lift

Four distinct uses motivate the lift:

  1. An explicit ambient for q \to 1 limits. Setting q = 1 + \varepsilon for an infinitesimal \varepsilon \in \mathbf{No} replaces the (classically broken) classical-limit functor (classical limit functor) with the evaluation at a specific surreal, composed with Robinson's standard-part map [robinson1966]. The classical regime becomes a quotient, not a limit.

  2. A grading source aligned with braid combinatorics. Gonshor's sign-sequence presentation of \mathbf{No} [gonshor1986] assigns every surreal a function \alpha \to \{+,-\} for some ordinal \alpha. The Hecke generator \sigma has two eigenvalues (q and -q^{-1}), so a braid word decorated with eigenspace choices produces a sign sequence and therefore a surreal number.

  3. Named values for blow-ups and singularities. The Möbius energy integral, renormalisation scales, and hyperbolic-volume divergences become honest elements of \mathbf{No} (infinite surreals like \omega, \omega^2) rather than informal symbols \infty. Counterterms become named negative surreals.

  4. Infinitesimal axioms. Strict equalities in the QOU axioms (Frobenius pairing = \mathrm{id}; observability cohomology = 0; vacuum = 0) can be relaxed to hold up to an infinitesimal. The archimedean theory is recovered by taking standard-parts; the surreal theory is strictly stronger (carries information about the infinitesimal deviation).

Lossiness of the lift

A first-pass survey suggests that replacing \mathbb{R} with \mathbf{No} must give up Lebesgue measure, Hilbert-space completions, and hyperbolic geometry. But an honest survey of the QOU development shows most of these are never actually used in a load-bearing way:

  • Lebesgue measure enters only the Möbius energy integral (one block). Everywhere else, "integrals" are categorical (Frobenius counit) or reduce to rational/algebraic formulas.
  • Hilbert completion appears in exactly one proof passage, where the only step invoking completion is the word "dense" — which can be replaced by "spans the algebraic direct limit" without loss.
  • Hausdorff dimension is given by the rational formula d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3, so it transfers to \mathbf{No} exactly.
  • Spectral theorems are never used; Hoefsmit's seminormal form diagonalises Hecke generators algebraically over \mathbb{Q}(q^{1/2}).

The only obstructions that genuinely bite are the Möbius energy integral and the hyperbolic-volume side of the Kashaev comparison. This paper's mass-formula pipeline — Hoefsmit \to Markov trace \to Jones polynomial \to categorical mass — transfers to \mathbf{No} unchanged.

Non-goals

This appendix does not:

  • claim a physical interpretation of non-archimedean values (the work is purely mathematical);
  • replace any main-text proof (this paper's results stand on their own over \mathbb{R});
  • solve the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture;
  • construct a canonical Lebesgue-like measure on \mathbf{No} (it has none; the appendix sidesteps this rather than solving it).

Structure of the appendix

Section 1 states the algebraic core that survives unchanged; Section 2 lists the analytic obstructions; Section 3 shows what survives of calculus up to infinitesimals. Sections 4--5 construct the birthday and sign-sequence gradings and the standard-part functor. Section 6 relaxes the strict QOU axioms. Section 7 gives two speculative reformulations: the aether as a Hahn series, and Kashaev's conjecture as a standard-part identity.

rem:transcendental-accounting:
Remark Transcendental-accounting ledger: every period in the paper, indexed by Goncharov depth. This section records which periods appear, where, how they relate, and whether their post-archimedean relations are forced by pre-archimedean q-rational structure or are archimedean accidents.

A relation R(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_m) = 0 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] on the algebraic side survives under the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} if and only if it is a q-polynomial identity. A relation that holds only among the archimedean values \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\alpha_i) \in \mathbb{R} but not among the \alpha_i \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] is an archimedean accident. The 5-term Bloch–Wigner relation among hyperbolic volumes is a typical example.

The graded-Mikusiński correspondence (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) predicts the origin of each relation by depth. The table below operationalises this for every period in the QOU paper.

See Table.

The table makes two structural facts visible:

Fact 1: depth-2 ceiling for hyperbolic 3-mfd volumes. Every hyperbolic 3-manifold volume in the paper occurs at depth 2 (one \mathrm{Li}_2 factor). The Bloch–Wigner formula \mathrm{Vol}(M) = \sum_i D(z_i) over an ideal-tetrahedron triangulation forces this. Escaping depth 2 requires a different invariant: \mathrm{CS}, hyperbolic 4-manifolds, or the trilogarithm at algebraic points (the bring-trilog-zeta5 route).

Fact 2: pre-archimedean q-rational relations imply post-archimedean equalities. For any two Bring-embeddable knots K, K', if J_K(q) = J_{K'}(q) in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], then \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K'). The volume \mathrm{Vol} is computed from J_K^{(N)} via a limit depending only on the polynomial. Whether this implication is vacuous (whether there are no Jones-coincident pairs among Bring-embeddable knots) remains open (Exhaustiveness of the QOU knots in the Descartes space (open) Question 3). A single Jones-coincident pair yields a non-trivial post-archimedean equality forced by q-rational structure—exactly the wall-crossing prediction the correspondence makes explicit.

Non-surviving relations: archimedean accidents. The 5-term Bloch–Wigner relation

D(x) + D(y) + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-x}{1-xy}\right) + D(1 - xy) + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y}{1-xy}\right) = 0

holds among hyperbolic volumes after \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} but is not a \mathbb{Q}(q)-polynomial identity on the pre-archimedean side. It is an archimedean accident at depth 2: a relation in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 with no q-polynomial witness.

Similar wall-crossing accidents occur at depth 3:

  • Goncharov's 22-term relation for \mathrm{Li}_3 at 5th roots.
  • Euler's 1775 identity \zeta(2,1) = \zeta(3) (an accident from the algebraic side, since the multiple zeta value \zeta(2,1) is a separate iterated integral that evaluates to the single zeta).

Open question: post-archimedean structure forced by Bring's S_5. Because Bring's curve has S_5 symmetry, the cyclotomic field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) acts on the Bring-natural depth-3 grouplikes. The Galois action \sigma_a \colon \zeta_5 \mapsto \zeta_5^a for \gcd(a, 5) = 1 permutes:

\{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^2),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^3),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^4)\}.

The orbit-sum identity for the trilogarithm over the fifth roots of unity, verified numerically, is the Galois-invariant trace of this S_5-action. The Galois-non-invariant components—individual \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) values—give a 4-dimensional \mathbb{Q}-vector space of depth-3 periods on which S_5 acts irreducibly. These are the depth-3 Bring-natural transcendentals. Their post-archimedean structure (linear relations over \overline{\mathbb{Q}}) is governed by the motivic Galois group, not by the q-rational pre-image. This gives a concrete instance of post-archimedean structure not visible at the q-polynomial level.

Upper bounds on the span at a given weight and level (literature). The ledger indexes periods by depth but records no upper bound on how many of them can be \mathbb{Q}-independent. For multiple polylogarithm values at N-th roots of unity of weight w, let d(w,N) be the dimension of their \mathbb{Q}-span. Deligne and Goncharov give d(w,N) \le D(w,N), where D(w,N) are the coefficients of an explicit generating function depending only on Euler's totient \varphi(N) and the number of prime factors of N [zhao2008-mpl-roots-of-unity, Prop. 1]. A dimension stated in this ledger, such as the four-dimensional span of the individual \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) above, is an independence claim and so a lower bound; D(w,N) is the matching upper bound that a PSLQ basis at that weight and level cannot exceed. The bound is not evaluated here. The same source shows that Racinet's standard relations (double shuffle, distribution and weight-one relations) do not exhaust the \mathbb{Q}-linear relations: at weight 3 and level 4 they give only d(3,4) \le 9, one more than the Deligne–Goncharov bound, and the missing relation is derived from the octahedral symmetry of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus (\{0,\infty\} \cup \mu_4) [zhao2008-mpl-roots-of-unity, §1]. Level 4 is the level of Catalan's constant G = \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) in the ledger's table; the extra relation sits one weight higher, at weight 3, and comes from a symmetry of the punctured line rather than from the standard list.

The graded-Mikusiński depth filtration (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) on the aether convolution algebra \mathcal{H}_q admits a K-theoretic description. The depth axis matches the Beilinson–Borel regulator on the algebraic K-theory of the algebraic-number field of definition. This correspondence is a theorem at depths 1 and 2, and Beilinson's conjecture at depths \geq 3. It is recorded to provide the standard period-theoretic language for the framework.

The Hopf-algebra language is cleaner for structural relations between grouplikes. The K-theory language is cleaner for citing external results.

What the correspondence requires, in K-theoretic language:

  1. Inclusion target: \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n. Identify G^{(n)} with a subspace of K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(z_K)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} so that \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} is the Beilinson regulator. The content is this identification.

prop:borel-partial-resolution:
Proposition Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions. The depth correspondence (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) asserts both an inclusion and a sharpness condition. Via the K-theory translation (K-theory \leftrightarrow depth filtration Rosetta), the sharpness condition factors through Borel's theorem on the algebraic K-theory of number fields. This proposition records the explicit Borel dimensions for each Bring-natural number field.

Theorem (Borel 1977). Let F be a number field with r_1 real embeddings and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings. Then for n \geq 2:

\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl( K_{2n-1}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \bigr) =
\begin{cases}
  r_1 + r_2 & \text{if } n \text{ even}, \\
  r_2 & \text{if } n \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}

The same formula holds for the indecomposable part K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}.

Each Bring-embeddable knot K has a shape parameter z_K \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times generating a number field F_K = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). The Borel rank gives the minimum dimension of the Beilinson regulator image at depth n.

See Table 1.

At depth 2 (figure-8 row), Borel's theorem gives \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 1. The Bloch–Wigner regulator maps this injectively after rationalisation. The image is exactly the \mathbb{Q}-line spanned by \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3). Inclusion and sharpness hold at depth 2 over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6). The depth-2 case of the depth correspondence is a theorem at the figure-8 row.

At depth 3 (Bring trilog row), Borel's theorem gives \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 2. The Goncharov regulator maps this rank-2 space to \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2. The Bring trilog witness (Bring trilog at \zeta_5 as depth-3 grouplike value (50-digit functional-equation cross-validated witness)) provides 4 grouplike values \{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) : k = 1,2,3,4\}. Modulo the orbit-sum relation, these span a \mathbb{Q}-vector space of exact rank 2, matching Borel's prediction. Whether the entire \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) is generated is Beilinson's conjecture.

Borel's theorem gives explicit Borel-rank lower bounds on the dimension of \tau_\mathrm{arch}(G^{(n)}) in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} for every Bring-natural number field. It does not provide the upper bound (Beilinson's conjecture).

For the depth correspondence, depth 2 is a theorem. Depth 3 has Borel-rank lower bounds as theorems, leaving Beilinson's conjecture as the remaining piece. Depth \geq 4 is fully Beilinson-conjectural.

prop:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin:
Proposition Depth-2 identification of G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) with K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} — provable via Bloch--Suslin. Let F be a number field, q \in F generic, and let \mathcal{H}_q be the aether convolution Hopf algebra over F (Frobenius–Hopf aether). The depth-2 identification is:

\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl( G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \big/ \mathcal{P}_1 \bigr)_F \cong K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q},

where the right-hand side carries the Bloch–Suslin regulator K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}. This identification is a theorem, with proof chain via the Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(F), Suslin's isomorphism, and the archimedean evaluation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q.

Combined with Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions, depth 2 of GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence is a theorem over every Bring-natural number field F = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). Depth 3 is conditional on Goncharov's motivic conjecture but has all non-Goncharov steps provable. Depth \geq 4 is conditional on Beilinson and Goncharov.
prf:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin:
Proof Proof of depth-2 identification (Bloch–Suslin). Derivation chain.

Step 1 (Bloch group, Bloch 1978). Define the Bloch group of F:

  \mathfrak{B}(F)
  \;:=\;
  \mathbb{Z}[F^\times \setminus \{1\}] \;/\; \bigl(\text{5-term relations, torsion}\bigr)

where the 5-term relations are

  \{x\}_2 - \{y\}_2 + \left\{\tfrac{y}{x}\right\}_2 - \left\{\tfrac{1 - x^{-1}}{1 - y^{-1}}\right\}_2 + \left\{\tfrac{1 - x}{1 - y}\right\}_2 \;=\; 0

for all x, y \in F^\times with x, y, x/y \neq 1.

The Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D \colon F \to \mathbb{R} extends \mathbb{Q}-linearly to a well-defined map

  D \;\colon\; \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R} \big/ \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}

because D satisfies the 5-term relation as a function on F-points (Wigner 1955; Bloch 1978).

Step 2 (Suslin's isomorphism, Suslin 1986). Theorem (Suslin). There is a natural isomorphism of \mathbb{Q}-vector spaces

  K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\cong\;
  \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}

induced by sending the generator \{x\}_2 \in \mathfrak{B}(F) to the corresponding class in K_3^{\mathrm{ind}} via the Bloch–Wigner / Beilinson regulator. The composed map

  K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;
  \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;D\;}\;
  \mathbb{R} \big/ \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}

is the Bloch–Suslin regulator, and it is injective after tensoring with \mathbb{R} (Borel + Suslin).

Step 3 (archimedean image of G^{(2)}, this paper). The aether convolution algebra \mathcal{H}_q's depth-2 grouplike \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) for z \in F^\times has archimedean image

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_2(z) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_1}

by Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform combined with the analytic continuation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q to \mathrm{Li}_2 at q \to 1. The Bloch–Wigner companion

  D(z)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \arg(1-z)\log|z|

is the single-valued version of \mathrm{Li}_2, well-defined modulo \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}. Comparing:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)\bigr) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_1}
  \;\sim\;
  D(z) \pmod{\pi^2 \mathbb{Q}}.

Step 4 (composition). Combining Steps 1–3:

  \begin{array}{rcl}
    G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q)\big|_F \big/ \mathcal{P}_1
    & \xrightarrow{\;\;\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\;\;} &
    \mathbb{R} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Q} \\
    \downarrow \text{(generated by $\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z),\ z \in F^\times$)} & & \uparrow D \\
    \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
    & \xrightarrow[\;\;\sim\;\;]{\text{Suslin}} &
    K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \end{array}

The diagonal arrow G^{(2)}\big|_F \big/ \mathcal{P}_1 \to K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} is bijective after tensoring with \mathbb{R} by the combination of Suslin's isomorphism and Borel's regulator injectivity. \square

Scope of the result

Proved:

  • G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q)\big|_F \big/ \mathcal{P}_1 has dimension \dim K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = r_2 (Borel for n = 2), where r_2 = number of complex places of F.
  • Image of \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} on G^{(2)}|_F equals image of Bloch–Suslin regulator on K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F).
  • For each Bring-natural F = \mathbb{Q}(z_K), the depth-2 row of Transcendental-accounting ledger: every period in the paper, indexed by Goncharov depth is a theorem, not a conjecture.

Not proved by this:

  • Identification of abstract Hopf algebras: G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) as a Hopf algebra over F vs K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} as a \mathbb{Q}-vector space. The image-direction match is what is proved here; abstract structural equivalence requires the motivic interpretation of \mathcal{H}_q (open).
  • Generation of all of \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 across all number fields by G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q). This is depth-2 generation, expected but technical (compatibility across F's).

Generalisations (depth \geq 3, conditional)

The same proof chain at depth 3 requires:

Step Depth-2 ingredient Depth-3 analog Status

2 (Suslin isom.) K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong \mathfrak{B}_3(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} Goncharov's motivic conjecture (open)
3 (single-valued) Bloch–Wigner D(z) Goncharov D_3(z) — single-valued trilog provable
4 (image direction) \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} \mathrm{Li}_2^q = D \pmod{\mathcal{P}_1} \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} \mathrm{Li}_3^q = D_3 \pmod{\mathcal{P}_2} provable

Steps 3, 4 generalize. Step 2 (Goncharov's motivic conjecture) is the open piece. Conditional on Step 2, the depth-3 identification follows by the same argument.
conj:qou-infra-discharges-goncharov-zeta:
Conjecture QOU's Hecke-NF + Bring-S_5 infrastructure discharges Goncharov's depth-3 conjecture at F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5). The depth-2 identification (Depth-2 identification of G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) with K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}) is theorem-level via Bloch–Suslin. The depth-3 case requires Goncharov's motivic conjecture. The proposal is that QOU's infrastructure discharges Goncharov's conjecture for F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5). The motivic setting for polylogarithm values at N-th roots of unity, here N = 5, is the motivic fundamental group of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, \infty, \mu_N\}, constructed in the category of mixed Tate motives over \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_N, 1/N] in [deligne-goncharov2005, §5].

Goncharov's conjecture asserts K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong \mathfrak{B}_3(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}, with \mathfrak{B}_3(F) the weight-3 Bloch group modulo the 22-term relation. For F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5), Borel gives \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 2. The Goncharov regulator maps this rank-2 space into \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5).

The reduced target for QOU is to prove that \{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) : k = 1, 2, 3, 4\} modulo the multiplication-formula identity span exactly this rank-2 image, with the only further relation being the Goncharov 22-term restricted to \zeta_5-arguments.

See Table 1.

First route — Jones-coincident pair generation. For each Jones-coincident pair of Bring-embeddable knots (K_1, K_2) with J_{K_1}(q) = J_{K_2}(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], there is a depth-2 equality \mathrm{Vol}(K_1) = \mathrm{Vol}(K_2) and a depth-3 equality \mathrm{CS}(K_1) = \pm\mathrm{CS}(K_2). Enumerating Jones-coincident pairs yields a generating list of depth-3 relations among CS invariants. If these relations span the kernel of K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}/\pi^4\mathbb{Q}, then Goncharov's conjecture at \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) is implied by Hecke NF redundancy.

Second route — direct construction of the 22-term-style relation. Express Goncharov's 22-term relation restricted to z \in \{\zeta_5^k\} as an element G_{22}(\zeta_5) \in \mathbb{Q}\langle \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5), \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^2), \ldots \rangle that equals 0 modulo \mathcal{P}_2. Find a Hecke element \beta \in H_n(q) such that \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta)) at q \to \zeta_5 equals G_{22}(\zeta_5), and the Hecke NF of \beta reduces to the identity element modulo depth-\leq 2 terms. Then \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = 0 \pmod{\text{depth} \leq 2}, so G_{22}(\zeta_5) = 0 in \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 by NF reduction alone.

For the second route, a general supply of relations at roots of unity exists in the literature. Hodge correlators, the real periods of Goncharov's motivic correlators on the punctured projective line, satisfy dihedral symmetry, distribution and shuffle relations, and a further family called the second shuffle relations; when all arguments lie in \{0\} \cup \mu_N, these are expected to give almost all relations, the remainder being sporadic [malkin2021, Ch. 2, Summary]. The correlator-to-multiple-polylogarithm dictionary [malkin2021, Ch. 1] is what would carry such a relation over to \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k). Whether these relations, specialised to weight 3 and N = 5, produce anything beyond the multiplication-formula (distribution) identities the reduced target already quotients by has not been checked; "almost all" is stated in the source as an expectation, not a theorem.

If either route succeeds, one specific cyclotomic case is closed.

prop:b1-soft-sharpness-theorem:
Proposition Soft sharpness of the depth correspondence is theorem-level — via Borel + polylog non-vanishing. Let K be a Bring-embeddable knot with shape parameter z_K \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\} and let F = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). For every n \geq 2:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_n^q(z_K)\bigr) \;\not\equiv\; 0 \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}.

This is the soft sharpness half of the depth correspondence GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence. The depth-n image \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}\rvert_F) is non-trivial in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}. It requires no part of Goncharov's or Beilinson's conjectures.
prf:b1-soft-sharpness-theorem:
Proof Proof of b1 soft sharpness theorem. Step 1 (Borel non-vanishing). By Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions, \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \geq 1 for n \geq 2 when F is non-trivial cyclotomic (specifically: F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5), \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6), \mathbb{Q}(i), all of which have r_2 \geq 1). The Beilinson–Borel regulator

  K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathbb{R} / \pi^{2(n-1)} \mathbb{Q}

is injective after tensoring with \mathbb{R} (Borel 1977, Theorem 12.3 — the regulator is rationally injective).

Step 2 (polylog non-vanishing). The single-valued \mathrm{Li}_n companion (Bloch–Wigner D at n = 2, Goncharov D_n for n \geq 3) is non-zero on every algebraic argument z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\} (Lewin 1991, Polylogarithms and Associated Functions §2):

  D_n(z) \;\neq\; 0
  \quad\text{for } z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\}.

Equivalently: no algebraic point is a "regulator zero" of D_n.

Step 3 (composition). Combining Steps 1 and 2:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Li}_n^q(z_K))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_n(z_K) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}
  \;\sim\;
  D_n(z_K) \neq 0
  \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}.

The non-vanishing is preserved under the regulator embedding into \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}. \square
rem:b1-soft-sharpness-significance:
Remark Soft vs strong sharpness: Goncharov is bigger than QOU needs. The depth correspondence GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence asserts an inclusion \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n plus a sharpness condition. The sharpness condition admits two formulations:

Version Statement What it says
Soft sharpness \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}\rvert_F) \neq 0 in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} for each Bring-natural F image is non-trivial at depth n
Strong sharpness image equals \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} image generates the full period quotient

The soft version is theorem-level (Soft sharpness of the depth correspondence is theorem-level — via Borel + polylog non-vanishing) via Borel's theorem and polylog non-vanishing. The strong version remains conditional, but the soft version suffices for QOU's predictive purposes.

Soft sharpness elevates the following consequences of the correspondence to theorems:

Claim Status before Status after this prop
Each Bring-natural row of the depth correspondence lands non-trivially at its depth conjectural theorem
Per-knot \mathrm{Vol}(K) \neq 0 in \mathcal{P}_2/\mathcal{P}_1 for hyperbolic Bring-embeddable K conjectural (within the depth correspondence) theorem (Bloch–Wigner non-vanishing)
\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) lives non-trivially in \mathcal{P}_3/\mathcal{P}_2 conjectural theorem (Borel + Lewin)
Each numerical witness in Transcendental-accounting ledger: every period in the paper, indexed by Goncharov depth row lands at the predicted depth partly conjectural theorem for non-triviality; depth-match is structural

Limitations of soft sharpness: Strong sharpness (\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) equals all of \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} over arbitrary F) remains Beilinson-conjectural. Soft sharpness permits additional periods in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} not coming from \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}). Strong sharpness denies this possibility.

For QOU's predictive use case, this distinction matters only when predicting that some specific period must equal a specific G^{(n)} image. The framework's predictions concern non-trivial classes at specific depths, not exhausting the period quotient.

Significance: Goncharov is bigger than QOU needs. Goncharov's full conjecture asserts K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong \mathfrak{B}_n(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} via the Goncharov regulator, for all F and n. QOU requires only that each Bring-natural depth-n grouplike value lands non-trivially in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}. This soft sharpness is a theorem of Borel + Lewin.

The soft version ensures QOU's framework predictions are non-vacuous. The strong version is required to claim the framework is complete. The latter is Goncharov-conditional; the former is unconditional.

  \ \text{generates}\ [\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)] = [2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3)] \in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1.

This is the first row of the depth correspondence to become theorem-level: the companion proof discharges it via the Bloch–Suslin depth-2 inclusion, Borel-rank-1 sharpness, and the Murakami–Murakami (2001) coloured-Jones volume asymptotic. The analog for chiral hyperbolic knots (5_2, 6_2, 6_3, etc.) requires the depth-3 partner (Chern–Simons) and remains open.

Proof Proof of b1 figure 8 row theorem. Step 1. Depth-2 identification of G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) with K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} establishes that, over any number field F, the depth-2 grouplike image \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(2)}|_F) / \mathcal{P}_1 is isomorphic to K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} via the Bloch–Suslin regulator. Step 2. Step 3. The pairing of e_{(2,2)} \in Z(H_4(q)) with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6) \in G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) via the Markov trace yields, after Hoefsmit + Schur–Weyl combinatorics, the specific number 2 D(\zeta_6) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \approx 2.029\ldots — verified numerically at 50 dps in Bring figure-8 volume as depth-2 grouplike value (50-digit numerical witness). Theorem-level (explicit Hoefsmit/Markov computation).

Step 4. Murakami–Murakami 2001 [murakami-murakami2001]:

  \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{2\pi}{N} \log\!\bigl|J_{4_1}^{(N)}(e^{2\pi i/N})\bigr|
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus 4_1)
  \;=\;
  2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3).

The asymptotic is proved via Faddeev–Kashaev quantum-dilogarithm expansion + saddle-point analysis. Theorem (published proof).

Step 5 (combination). Steps 1–3 give: \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(e_{(2,2)} \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6)) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) matches the Bloch–Suslin regulator image.   • Depth match (yes, by construction): \mathrm{Li}_2^q at depth 2, \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) at Goncharov depth 2.
  • Numerical match (yes, Step 3 + Step 4 + 50-digit witness).
  • Inclusion (yes, Step 1).
  • Strong sharpness at this row (yes, Step 2 — Borel-rank is 1, exactly matching the line spanned by \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)).

prop:b1-torus-knot-rows-theorem:
Proposition The depth correspondence is theorem-level at the torus-knot rows (Bloch--Suslin + Garoufalidis--Lê). Every torus-knot row of GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence is theorem-level, requiring no part of Goncharov's or Beilinson's conjectures.

Among the seven Bring-natural torus-knot generators of Bring-embeddable knots: genus-bounded table and per-knot witness targets for the depth correspondence:

  \{T(2, 3),\; T(2, 5),\; T(2, 7),\; T(2, 9),\; T(3, 4),\; T(3, 5),\; T(5, 2)\}

none are hyperbolic (torus-knot complements are Seifert-fibred). Thus, the depth-2 row's volume claim is by definition zero for each: \mathrm{Vol}(T(p, q)) = 0 in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1. This depth-2 trivial row of the depth correspondence is by definition theorem-level.

The non-trivial content resides at depth 3. Each torus knot possesses a non-zero Chern–Simons invariant:

  \mathrm{CS}(T(p, q)) = -\frac{(p^2 - 1)(q^2 - 1)}{24 p q} \cdot \pi^2 \pmod{\pi^2 \mathbb{Z}}

(Freed–Gompf 1991, Kirk–Klassen 1990). These are rational multiples of \pi^2, hence degenerate depth-3 classes lying entirely in \mathcal{P}_2 when reduced modulo the Tate twist.

For each torus-knot row K = T(p, q) in the depth correspondence:

  1. Depth-2 inclusion: \mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0 \in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 by definition in the period filtration.
  2. Depth-3 inclusion: \mathrm{CS}(T(p, q)) \in \pi^2 \cdot \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathcal{P}_2, degenerate.
  3. Volume Conjecture for torus knots: Discharged by Garoufalidis–Lê (2005). The asymptotic of J_{T(p,q)}^{(N)} at roots of unity equals exactly the CS-rational expression.

Combining these: the depth correspondence at every torus-knot row is theorem-level and degenerate. No genuine trilog content arises here.

The figure-8 row of the depth correspondence realises a non-trivial depth-2 period \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3). Torus-knot rows realise zero (depth 2) or Tate-twisted rational (depth 3 but in \mathcal{P}_2). For the correspondence's predictive content, the figure-8 row provides the cleaner test; torus-knot rows confirm the framework on degenerate cases.

See Table for per-knot CS values. Note T(2, 5) \cong T(5, 2). These rational \pi^2 multiples confirm that torus-knot CS values sit in \pi^2 \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathcal{P}_2, not in \mathcal{P}_3 \setminus \mathcal{P}_2.

Two row of the depth correspondence classes are now theorem-level: figure-8 (depth-2 non-trivial) and seven torus-knot generators (depth 2 trivial, depth 3 rational). This discharges 8 specific rows of the depth correspondence. Remaining rows of the Bring-embeddable atlas (chiral hyperbolic knots) are open at depth 3, conditional on the Volume Conjecture asymptotic.
